The Special Land Acquisition Officer (here-in-after referred as SLAO), KIADB (Metro Rail Project),
Bengaluru, has sent this reference under Sections 30 and 31(2) of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (here-in-after referred as L.A. Act, 1894), for apportionment of compensation amount.

.2. The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No. 41/3A measuring 144 sq. meters situated in ward No. 131 of Nayandanahalli village, within the jurisdiction of BBMP has been acquired for the purpose of Bengaluru Metro Rail Project.
Preliminary notification was issued on 30.08.2013.
Final notification was issued on 29.12.2014.
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 22.01.2016 fixing compensation of Rs.53,16,170/-.

In-spite of service of notice, title documents were not produced and so the L.A.O. has sent the reference and deposited a sum of Rs. 42,52,936/- after deducting 20% income tax of Rs.
-4- : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
10,63,234/-.
The above amount has been kept in F.D. in SBI, Cauvery Bhavan Branch, Bengaluru.
.3. After receipt of reference, this court has registered the case and issued notice to both parties and claimants 2 to 5 have appeared before the Court through their counsels.
The claimant No. 1 did not appear before this Court and hence, he has been placed exparte.

sentences.text: The claimants 2 to 5 have filed claim statement stating that the site bearing Sy.No. 41/3 of Nayandanahalli village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka measuring East to West 60 feet and North to South 212 feet was purchased by Azeezulla Khan @ Adil Pasha who is the father of claimants 2 to 5 under a registered sale deed dated 23.06.1981.
Subsequent to purchase of the said property, the father of claimant No. 2 to 5 was in possession and enjoyment of the said property.

It is stated that their father Azeezulla Khan @ Adil Pasha gifted the southern portion of the said property measuring 50 X 212 feet to claimant No. 2 to 5 -5- : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
under a registered gift deed dated 16.01.2014. and the remaining northern portion has been gifted to uncle of claimants 2 to 5 namely Nazeer Khan and Eliaz Khn under gift deed dated 16.01.2014.
It is stated that the southern portion of the schedule property measuring 50 X 40 feet in all measuring 2000 sq. feet has been acquired for Metro Rail Project.

On account of formation of Metro Rail project and erection of High tension tower, the claimants unable to use / put up either any residential or commercial construction in order to utilize the property for better use on the schedule property and same became useless.

.5. It is stated that the claimants 2 to 5 came to know only when workers of Metro Rail project were making construction on their land and then only they came to know their lands has been notified in the acquisition proceedings and the name of claimant No. 1 Syed Aslam has been shown as notified khathedar.

It is stated that the claimant No.1 has no subsisting right over the said land since he had sold the same under -6- : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
registered sale deed dated 23.06.1981.

Hence, prayed to grant compensation in-favour of claimants 2 to 5.
.6.
In order to prove their case, the claimant No. 5 has been examined as PW.1.
The Special Power of Attorney holder of claimants 2 to 5 has been examined as PW.1.
The evidence of PW.1 has been discarded.

The documents got marked Exs.P.1 to 15.
.7.
Heard the arguments.

.8. The following points that would arise for my consideration are:
1) Which of the claimants are entitled to receive the compensation amount?
2) What order or award?
.9.

Point No.1 : As per discussion Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS
.10. POINT NO.1: The Special Power of Attorney holder of claimants 2 to 5 i.e., Azeezulla Khan @ Adil -7- : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
Pasha has been examined as PW.2.

He has stated that Sy.No. 41/3 totally measuring 2 acres 35 guntas originally belongs to Vimala Prabhakar who purchased from Shivaram Devarao Ubhayakar under the registered sale deed dated 06.01.1972.
PW.2 has stated that out of 2 acres 35 guntas Smt. Vimala Prabhakar sold an extent of 38 guntas to one Syed Aslam S/o S.A. Khader under a registered sale deed dated 15.02.1975.
Ex.P.8 is the sale deed.
From Ex.P.8 it is seen that Syed guntas.

PW.2 has stated that out of 38 guntas in Sy.No. 41/3 Syed Aslam formed sites and sold site No.
2 to an extent of 60 X 212 feet in his favour under a registered sale deed dated 23.06.1981.
Ex.P.1 is the irrevocable General Power of Attorney.
Under the document PW.2 has been given all power to deal with property measuring 60 X 212 feet in-respect of Sy.No. 41/3.
PW.2 has stated that subsequent to the purchase, he has been assessed for tax and paying taxes.

He was in possession and enjoyment of the property by exercising -8- : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
all acts of ownership.
Ex.P.2 is the House list assessment extract.
From the document it is seen that name of Azeezulla Khan @ Adil Pasha entered in anubhavadar column.
Ex.P.3 is the Encumbrance certificate for the period from 01.07.1981 to 31.03.1989 in-respect of site No. 2 measuring 60 X 212 feet of Nayandanahalli village,which discloses nil encumbrance.
.11. PW.2 has stated that he gifted the southern portion of the said property measuring 50 X 177 feet in- favour of claimants 2 to 5 under a registered gift deed dated 16.01.2014.
Ex.P.7 is the said gift deed.
From the document, it is seen that PW.2 has gifted site No. 2 measuring 50 X 177 feet in all measuring 8850 sq. feet to claimants 2 to 5.

PW.2 has stated that claimants 2 to 5 are his own children; that southern portion of the schedule property measuring 50 X 40 feet in all measuring 2000 sq. feet has been acquired for Metro Rail project.

On account of formation of Metro Rail project he is unable to use the remaining extent of the -9- : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
schedule property since high voltage electricity is running on the metro line.

PW.2 has stated that on account of implementation of Metro Rail project in the schedule property the entire land has become useless and he is unable to utilize the entire schedule property either for residential or commercial purpose.

Ex.P.9 to 13 are five Syed Aslam vs Unknown on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194053941/
4 tax paid receipts in-respect of acquired land.
Ex.P.14 is the Encumbrance certificate from 01.04.2013 to 17.02.2020.

From Ex.P.7 document, it is seen that the gift made by PW.2 in-favour of claimants 2 to 5 on 16.01.2014.
.12.
During cross-examination PW/2 has stated that Syed Aslam was not his relative and that he had sold the property to him.
Syed Aslam has been referred to as claimant No. 1 in this case.
He has remained exparte in-spite of service of notice.
From Ex.P.1 it is clear that in view of irrevocable power of attorney executed by Syed Aslam in-favour of PW.2, the claimant No. 1 has lost his title to the acquired property.

It is elicited that originally the property came within the - 10 - : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
limits of Group panchayath and thereafter has come within the limits of BBMP.
PW.2 has stated that on account of high voltage electricity, the BBMP has not made the khatha in-respect of the property.
He has stated that they came to know about the acquisition when the JCB was brought to the property.
.13. From the oral and documentary evidence, it is clear that the claimants 2 to 5 are the owners of the acquired extent of 144 sq. meters.
As their property has been acquired, they are together entitled for compensation amount.
The claimants 2 to 5 have sought for compensation in-respect of remaining extent of property as property as the land has become useless in view of passing of high voltage electricity.
This Court can only appropriate the compensation amount which is deposited.
It is open for the claimants 2 to 5 to seek for the relief before proper Forum if they are aggrieved on account of acquisition.
Accordingly, the point No.1 for consideration is answered partly in the affirmative.

In view of my finding on the above point No.1, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The reference made by the respondent No.1/S.L.A.O. under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 is hereby partly allowed.

Claimants 2 to 5 are together  entitled to receive the compensation amount in respect of property bearing Sy.No. 41/3A measuring 144 sq. meters situated in Ward No. 131 of Nayandanahalli village within the jurisdiction of BBMP,
along with accrued interest thereon.

Claimants 2 to 5 shall have to execute indemnity bonds with one surety, undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in this court or in any other court, if Syed Aslam vs Unknown on 13 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194053941/
5 ordered to do so, which amount they are going to receive in this case.
The reference made by the respondent No.1/ S.L.A.O., in-respect of claimant No. 1 is rejected.
- 12 - : L.A.C. No.66/2016:
Draw award accordingly.
